answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, making influence on a sybil set proportional to its probability of escaping. When adversarial identities form a sparse external cut with low conductance, Φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), walk mass remains trapped inside S; min-cut transitivity bounds thus cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight despite unlimited internal endorsements. Names such as grove, comet, and lotus cannot increase that bound.
